plugins.title: Hexed
plugins.description: Roll a look onto any picture or clip. Hexed picks a grade, a print screen, lens effects, tape damage and a camera shake. Keep the parts you like and reroll the rest.
plugins.intro: A look is eleven slots, each holding one named effect. Roll a number and every slot fills. The same number always gives the same look, so a render comes out the same every time.

features.text: One number picks a crop, a grade, a print screen, lens effects, tape damage and a camera shake. Roll again for a different look.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/kinetic-typography
plugins.title: Kinetic typography
plugins.description: Captions that move with the voice, in fourteen ready-made styles. A hook word is set huge, and handwritten captions can follow a tracked subject.
plugins.intro: Captions sets a voiceover on screen. Each word arrives as it is said and the line leaves all together. A line with a big word is a hook: that word is set huge and the small words sit round it. HandCaptions writes the other way, one letter at a time in mixed handwriting.

features.title: Fourteen caption styles
features.text: Highlighter, typewriter, a text-selection sweep, a shine, a difference-blend prism and more. Pick one by name, then change its fonts, motion and colours. The accent colour and a readable shadow can come from your footage.

features.title: Hand captions
features.text: Each word writes itself across the time it is spoken, one letter at a time, every letter in a different handwritten face. Key words break out in a fat serif or a heavy italic, each with its own colour if you like. A dark halo keeps the letters readable over bright footage.

clip.caption: A line written centred low on archive film.

features.title: Follows a tracked subject
features.text: The text hangs beside the subject, on the side with room. A reticle frames the subject and a bracket marks the letter being written. Give it the subject's box and the text stays clear of it.

clip.caption: A line written beside a tracked anvil.

studio.panel: Studio gets a Captions panel: a card for each style drawn in its own type, a Caption or Big text switch for font, case, weight, size, tracking and colour, layout cards, motion controls with an In and Out switch, and an accent colour you can take from the footage. studio.note: There are no agent tools. The skill tells an agent to take word timestamps from your speech-to-text or voice-over tool instead of placing frames by hand, choose the lines and the big words, and render a settled hook frame and caption frame to check that both read. For tracked text it tracks the subject with the VJ plugin.

plugins.description: Give a video the feel of real paper. Keyword match cuts, photo cut-outs that unfold from a crumpled packet, and hand-drawn lines round a moving subject on torn paper.
plugins.intro: Paper brings creases, scanned fibres and grain to a video. From them it makes keyword match cuts, photo cut-outs and hand-drawn lines on torn paper.

features.text: A highlighted keyword holds still while the page under it changes several times a second. Use made-up pages or your own screenshots.

clip.caption: The web look, keyword Super Bowl.

features.title: CutOut and FoldOut
features.text: A photo with its background removed becomes a paper cut-out. FoldOut opens it from a crumpled packet, in stop motion.

clip.caption: A cut-out opening on a desk.

features.title: Scrapline
features.text: A marker, pencil, crayon, scribble or brush line is drawn round a moving subject, on torn paper. It redraws a few times a second, like hand animation.

plugins.title: VJ
plugins.description: Make footage look like a CRT, a worn VHS tape, a thermal camera or a 1-bit screen. Track what moves and draw boxes on it, cut a person into a pop-art poster, or fly a camera through clips seen as windows.
plugins.intro: VJ makes a picture look like it came from a screen, a tape or a sensor. Brightness stands in for heat and depth, so these are looks, not measurements. It also draws tracking marks on whatever moves, cuts a person into a pop-art poster and builds a camera fly-through of clips.

features.title: Screens and tapes
features.text: A CRT with curved glass that switches off, a worn VHS tape, a 1-bit screen, and a pixel magnifier that resolves into red, green and blue stripes.

clip.caption: A CRT tube switching off, on archive film.

features.title: Thermal and depth
features.text: Brightness becomes a thermal-camera palette or a depth-map look.

clip.caption: A thermal palette over a parade.

features.title: Flash looks
features.text: Acid heat, night vision, screen glow and grainy black and white, to cut on the beat.

clip.caption: Flash looks on a song, each held for a second and a half.

features.title: PopArt
features.text: Footage of a person cuts to an anime poster of them: blue tones, ink lines and rim light over a halftone. It needs a matte of the person, which a bundled tool makes once per clip.

clip.caption: Fred Ott cut to an anime poster and back.

features.title: Tracking
features.text: A tracker runs once and saves where things moved. Blobs draws boxes and links on every frame. Reticle marks one point.

features.title: Fragments
features.text: Clips show only through windows: boxes round the people and animals in them, tiles of sky, round holes. Each clip sits on its own plane at its own depth, and a camera flies through so near pieces slide past faster than far ones. Boxes carry name tags with a flickering confidence figure. Whoever edits the video names the boxes; no detection model runs.

components.title: Screenshot card burst
components.description: A wordmark fades in on black, then a cluster of screenshot cards bursts out of one point as the camera flies in. The cards settle into a dense wall, drift, and whip off to the right. Big white type finishes it: two short lines, each starting as a single word.
change: The brand name and the word after it in the wordmark (or none), and the two closing lines.
Your own screenshots or photos on the cards, and the words printed on the cards. With none, every card is drawn.
The three typefaces (wordmark and cards, terminal, serif) and the colours: canvas, text, accent, paper and dark cards.
The seed, which sets the tilt and timing of the burst.

components.title: App window greeting
components.description: A gradient wordmark on a soft off-white ground shrinks away as an app window grows in behind it. The camera pushes into the window, tilted, and types a greeting and a question in large perspective type. Four suggestion cards slide in, then the camera pulls back and flattens to the whole window.
change: The brand name, the name in the greeting, the question under it and the placeholder in the prompt box.
One to four suggestion cards, with your own labels, and the small caption at the bottom (or none).
The typeface, and the colours: ground, glows, window, cards, text and the wordmark and greeting gradients.
Whether it moves in two-frame steps or smoothly at 60 frames a second.

components.title: Social post on a phone
components.description: A phone showing a social post starts as a close-up of its lower edge, pulls back and glides to rest. Chat bubbles, avatars and icon chips pop in around it. A hand reaches into the photo and lifts the phone, and the screen swaps to a second one as the view count reaches its cap.
change: The brand name in the post header, the caption pill and the two-part subtitle on the photo.
The view count: where it starts, where it stops, and its unit.
The three chat bubbles, and the words on the second screen.
Your own photo for the post, a second picture for the swap, a logo and four avatars. Without them, all of it is drawn.
The typefaces and colours, and whether the motion steps at 24 frames a second or runs smooth at 60.

components.title: Chat prompt to reply
components.description: A chat prompt types itself into a rounded box and sends. The shot cuts to the reply, built on a page the camera scrolls through. Two activity rows, a status line, a serif reply, a brand chip, a small table and a row of action icons fade up one after another.
change: The prompt, the two activity rows, the status line and the reply.
The brand chip, and the table: three column heads and one row.
The three typefaces (interface, mono chip, serif reply).
The colours: background, panel, text, the warm typing tint, labels, links and icons.

components.title: Scrapline cut-outs
components.description: A hand-drawn border round a cut-out subject, on a sheet of torn paper. The line can be a wobbly marker, pencil, crayon, scribble or brush. Line and paper redraw a few times a second, like hand animation.
change: The subject: a video with a black and white matte, a video with alpha, an image with alpha, or an SVG path.
The line style (Marker, Pencil, Crayon, Scribble or Brush), the paper (White, Kraft, Binder, Cardboard, your own picture or none), the line colour, the gap to the subject and the seed.

components.title: Two lines on a focus pull
components.description: Seven photo cards float round the edges of a near-black frame, out of focus. The camera pulls back and racks focus. A first line comes up out of the blur and a second line replaces it. The scene slides off to the right as the left card sharpens.
change: The two lines, and a product name in the second.
Your own photos on the seven cards. Any card you leave out keeps its drawn picture.
The typeface, weight, size, tracking and text colour, and the two colours of the background.
How strong the focus blur, the film grain and the closing slide are, and the frame where the first line gives way to the second.

components.title: Words cut to the beat
components.description: A 9.4 second black-and-white type spot, cut on every hit of its track. Each cut shows one word or a two-word lockup on a ground that flips between black and white. A last word types on, then blurs away.
change: The words: an intro, a run with one word per cut, and an outro. The word count has to match the number of cuts.
The track. A small tool finds its strongest hits and gives you the cuts.
The typeface. Another face lands in the same places.
